About the fixture bakery

The title of this page is one word, on purpose: the entry page has a good one, this page does not, and a sampling run has to end up with the worse of the two. Aggregation used to take the verdict from the worst page and the measurement from the entry page, which printed a passing number underneath a failing verdict.

Everything else here is ordinary: a canonical, a description, one heading, and prose long enough not to trip the thin-page warning.

Who writes here

A Baker keeps the culture, runs the ovens six mornings a week, and writes these pages. Before the bakery there were eleven years in restaurant kitchens, four of them in bread specifically. Nothing here is theoretical: every timing published on this site is one we work to, and when a timing changes we change the page and note the date on it. That is also why this fixture carries a byline at all — the E-E-A-T checks look for one, and a fixture that cannot satisfy them cannot demonstrate that they work.

How we test what we publish

A method reaches this site after we have used it for at least two months in production. Flour behaves differently between harvests, so a schedule that worked one autumn may need adjusting the next, and we would rather publish a range than a false precision. Where a claim depends on temperature we give the temperature; where it depends on a specific flour we name the flour.

Corrections

If something here is wrong, write to the address on the privacy page and we will correct it and say what changed. Two corrections were made this year: a hydration figure quoted for the wrong flour, and a proofing time that assumed a warmer kitchen than most people have. Both are noted on the pages themselves rather than quietly edited, because a correction nobody can see is indistinguishable from never having been wrong.
